idiom_name: .editorconfig formatting options applied by dotnet format (Allman braces, four-space block indent, braces-by-preference)
implementation_notes: C# answers the pattern with configuration instead of convention: the C# formatting options live in .editorconfig (indent_size = 4, csharp_new_line_before_open_brace = all, csharp_indent_block_contents = true, csharp_prefer_braces) and 'dotnet format whitespace' applies them mechanically, so the rectangle is a checked-in file plus a CI step; Microsoft's coding conventions state the same rules by hand (four spaces, no tabs, Allman braces, braces omissible only when every branch is single-line). What replaces the classic structure: csharp_prefer_braces plus early returns keep bodies one level deep, and switch expressions and 'is' patterns flatten type dispatch that used to be nested if/else rectangles. Keep the hand-applied form only where no .editorconfig is in scope (scripts, samples) and then follow the file being edited.
pitfalls: The preserve-single-line options decide whether a one-statement body may stay on the header line; leaving them unset makes formatter output flip per file and per editor.
dotnet format applies the nearest .editorconfig, so a repository hierarchy with conflicting files formats different projects differently - keep the shape rules in the root file.
Visual Studio or Rider 'format on save' with a different profile than CI produces a diff on every commit; import the same profile everywhere.
